chunks: Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to me from Abdallah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Yahya ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn Talha, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"By He who raised me as a bringer of glad tidings in truth, Allah will never punish a monotheist with the Fire forever, and the people of tawhid will intercede and their intercession will be accepted."

Then he (peace be upon him) said: "Verily, when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will command a people whose deeds were evil in the abode of this world to the Fire. They will say: 'O our Lord! How could You bring us into the Fire when we would declare Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our tongues with the Fire when they spoke of Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our hearts when they pledged that there is no god but You? How could You burn our faces when we placed them in the dust for You? How could You burn our hands when we raised them in supplication to You?'"

So Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, will say: 'My servants! Your deeds were evil in the abode of the world, so the Fire of Hell is your recompense.' So they will say: 'O our Lord! Is Your forgiveness greater, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, My forgiveness.' They will say: 'Is Your mercy vaster, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, My mercy.' They will say: 'Is our declaration of Your oneness greater, or our sins?' He will say: 'Rather, your declaration of My oneness is greater.' So they will say: 'O our Lord! Let Your forgiveness and Your mercy, which have encompassed all things, encompass us.'

So Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, will say: 'My angels! By My glory and My majesty, I have not created any creation more beloved to Me than those who declare My oneness and that there is no god besides Me. It is My responsibility not to commit the people of My tawhid to the Fire. Enter Paradise, My servants!'

key_terms.التوحيد: tawhid — the declaration of divine unity; here used as a basis for intercession and ultimate salvation
key_terms.الرحمة: rahma — mercy; God's mercy encompasses all things (cf. Quran 7:156)
key_terms.الشفاعة: shafa'a — intercession; the people of tawhid intercede and their intercession is granted
key_terms.العفو: 'afw — forgiveness/pardon; God's forgiveness is greater than any sin
key_terms.الموحد: muwahhid — one who affirms divine unity; the subject of God's mercy

ai.seo_question: Will those who affirmed God's oneness (tawhid) be forgiven on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) via Ibn 'Abbas and the Tabi'i scholar 'Ikrima, presents a profound eschatological dialogue on the Day of Judgment. The Prophet swears that no true monotheist will be eternally punished in the Fire, and the matn depicts a moving intercession scene where people whose worldly deeds were sinful appeal to God on the basis of their tawhid. God responds by affirming that His forgiveness and mercy surpass all sins, and that the declaration of His oneness is the greatest thing a servant can offer. The hadith reflects early Shia theological concerns about the salvific power of sincere tawhid and divine clemency, and was preserved in al-Saduq's Amali in the context of assemblies teaching core creedal doctrines.

and their intercession will be accepted

en.bilal-muhammad: Hamza b. Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Zayd b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim informed me. He said: Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to me from `Abdullah b. Hammad al-Ansari from al-Husayn b. Yahya b. al-Husayn from `Amr b. Talha from Asbat b. Nasr from `Ikrama from Ibn `Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
By He who raised me as a bringer of glad tidings in truth, Allah will never punish a monotheist. The people of monotheism will seek intercession and be interceded.

Then, he (as) said: Surely, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will order a people to the Fire whose deeds were evil in the abode of this world. They will say: “O Lord! How could You bring us into the Fire when we would declare Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our tongues in the Fire when they spoke of Your oneness in the world? How could You burn our hearts when they pledged that there is no god but You? How could You burn our faces when we placed them in the dust for You? How could You burn our hands when we raised them in supplication to You?”

So, Allah will say: “My worshipers! Your actions were evil in the abode of the world, so the Fire of Hell is your recompense.” So, they will say: “O Lord! What is greater: Your forgiveness, or our mistakes?” So, He will say: “My forgiveness, of course.” So, they will say: “What is vaster: Your mercy, or our sins?” So, He will say: “My mercy, of course.” So, they will say: “What is greater: our declaration of Your oneness, or our sins?” So, He will say: “Your declaration of My oneness, of course.” So, they will say: “O Lord! Embrace us with Your forgiveness and Your mercy, which have encompassed all things.”

So, Allah will say: “My angels! By My glory and My majesty, I have not created anything more beloved to Me than those who declare My oneness and that there is no god besides Me. It is My responsibility to not connect the people of My monotheism to the Fire. Bring My worshipers into Paradise.”
